readout_other: two-photon calcium imaging (GCaMP6f/tdTomato) of Gad2-positive interneurons
direction_notes: A subset of inhibitory interneurons showed an increase in calcium signal during 10 s stimulation; integrated activation increased sigmoidally with stimulation duration (1 to 20 s) and was significant for stimulation longer than 10 s.
safety_notes: No significant temperature rise (<0.1 C) was measured with a tissue phantom at the focus during increasing stimulation periods.

exposures.label: Acousto-optic window (implanted transparent PVDF-TrFE transducer) on somatosensory cortex

timing.protocol_description: 10 MHz, PRF 1.5 kHz, duty cycle 50 %, with 'pulse length' of 1 to 20 s (Fig. 3b); stimulation periods of 1, 5, 10 and 20 s were compared. The transducer sat directly on the cortex after open craniotomy.

source_quotes.n_subjects: (c) The integrated neuronal activation in response to varying stimulation periods from 1 to 20 s (n 34, 17, 84, and 48 neurons for 1, 5, 10, and 20 s, respectively; green dot: mean, whisker: SEM, acquired from three mice).

source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: Here, we propose a solution to this technical challenge by introducing an optically transparent acoustic transducer, termed the acousto-optic window (AOW).

flags.reason: 'Pulse length' in the Fig. 3b caption is 1 to 20 s, i.e. the stimulation train, not the individual pulse. Individual pulse duration is not stated (DC/PRF would be about 0.33 ms; not computed).

Abstract gives 0.035 MPa 'corresponding to 10 mW/cm2' without saying which intensity metric; the stated pressure is not tied to water or tissue. 10 mW/cm2 was not recorded. Hydrophone measurements in water (e.g. 0.11 MPa axial maximum at 60 Vpp, 3 cycles) used different drive settings.
Three mice stated for the stimulation-duration experiment; total number of mice used for Fig. 4b not given.
Transducer fabricated by the authors (PVDF-TrFE and ITO on a coverslip); the transducer is implanted on the cortex after craniotomy, not transcranial.
10 MHz recorded as 10000 kHz; pulse-echo centre frequency of the device was 24 MHz, with the 10 MHz being the lowest usable -6 dB frequency.
